examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 오늘 경기를 순연했어요.
examples.en: We postponed today's game because of the heavy rain.

examples.ko: 회사에서 행사 날짜를 다음 주로 순연하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to postpone the event to next week.
I heard they are postponing the show by a day because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 일정을 순연하면 예약도 다시 해야 해요.
examples.en: If we postpone the schedule, we have to make the reservation again.
The weather is bad, so would it be okay to postpone the departure?
What was the reason for postponing the game?

explain: '연기하다'와 비슷하지만 경기나 행사 일정을 그대로 뒤로 미룰 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '미루다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is similar to '연기하다' (to postpone) but often appears in the news when a game or event schedule is pushed back as it is. In daily talk, '미루다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 올해 회사의 순익이 작년보다 두 배 늘었어요.
examples.en: The company's net profit this year doubled compared to last year.

examples.ko: 세금을 빼고 나면 순익은 얼마 안 남아요.
examples.en: After taxes, there isn't much net profit left.
Have you calculated the shop's net profit?

examples.ko: 이번 분기 순익이 크게 줄었다고 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news said this quarter's net profit dropped a lot.
They shared half of the net profit with the employees.
Even if business is good, it's no use without net profit.

explain: '순이익'을 줄인 말이에요. '매출'이나 '수입'은 번 돈 전체를 말하고, 순익은 비용과 세금을 빼고 실제로 남은 돈을 말할 때 써요. 뉴스나 회사 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '순이익'. '매출' and '수입' mean the money earned in total, while 순익 is what actually remains after costs and taxes. It often appears in the news and in business talk.

examples.ko: 아이의 순진무구한 웃음을 보면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Seeing a child's innocent smile makes my heart feel at ease.

examples.ko: 동생은 아직도 순진무구해서 거짓말을 잘 믿어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is still so naive that they easily believe lies.
The puppy looks at me with innocent eyes.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 순진무구한 역할을 정말 잘 해요.
examples.en: That actor plays innocent roles really well.
I wish I could stay innocent even after I grow up.

examples.ko: 그렇게 순진무구하게 말하면 아무도 화를 못 내요.
examples.en: If you speak so innocently, nobody can get angry.

explain: '순진하다'보다 더 강하고 글 같은 느낌이에요. 때 묻지 않은 아이나 동물에게 쓰면 좋은 뜻이지만, 어른에게 쓰면 세상 물정을 모른다는 놀림처럼 들릴 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is stronger and more literary than '순진하다'. It is a compliment for children or animals, but said about an adult it can sound like teasing that they don't know the world.

examples.en: A fair wind blew, and the boat moved quickly.

examples.ko: 오늘은 순풍 덕분에 자전거 타기가 힘들지 않았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the tailwind, cycling wasn't hard today.
The yacht runs across the sea on a fair wind.

examples.ko: 처음엔 순풍이 불더니 갑자기 바람이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: At first there was a fair wind, but suddenly the wind changed.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 순풍이 불어 줘서 걷기 편했어요.
examples.en: A tailwind was blowing from behind, so walking was comfortable.

examples.ko: 이 항구는 순풍이 부는 날에 배가 많이 떠나요.
examples.en: Many ships leave this port on days with a fair wind.

explain: 가려는 방향으로, 뒤에서 불어 주는 바람이에요. 반대말은 '역풍'이고, 일이 잘 풀릴 때 비유로도 써요.

phrases.example: 새 가게가 순풍에 돛 단 듯 잘되고 있어요.
phrases.en: The new shop is doing well, like a ship with its sails up in a fair wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 막힘없이 아주 잘 풀릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things go very smoothly without any obstacles.

explain_en: It is a wind that blows from behind, in the direction you are going. Its opposite is '역풍', and it is also used figuratively when things go well.

examples.en: The singer started a nationwide tour.
I heard the tour tickets are already sold out.

examples.ko: 극단은 일 년 내내 순회공연을 다녀요.
examples.en: The theater troupe goes on tour all year round.
On this tour, they are coming to our city too.
The singer came back to Korea after finishing the tour.

examples.ko: 우리 학교에도 순회공연을 하러 오면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope they come to our school to perform on their tour.

explain: 여러 지역을 돌며 하는 공연이에요. 요즘 가수 이야기에서는 '투어'나 '전국 투어'라는 말도 많이 써요. '순회공연을 하다/다니다/마치다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a performance given while traveling through several regions. In talk about singers, people also say '투어' or '전국 투어'. It is used as '순회공연을 하다/다니다/마치다'.

examples.en: The classroom buzzed at the sudden news.
People started to murmur restlessly.

examples.ko: 선거 결과가 나오자 회사 분위기가 술렁거려요.
examples.en: The mood at the company is unsettled now that the election results are out.
I don't know why everyone is so restless.
The buzzing audience quickly became quiet.
My mind was stirred up, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: '술렁이다', '술렁대다'와 뜻이 거의 같아요. 사람들이 놀라거나 불안하거나 들떠서 웅성웅성할 때 써요. 마음에도 쓸 수 있지만 보통은 모인 사람들이나 분위기에 써요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '술렁이다' and '술렁대다'. It is used when people are surprised, anxious or excited and start to murmur. It can describe a mind too, but usually it describes a crowd or an atmosphere.

examples.en: The village was stirred up when the rumor spread.
The students are buzzing about the exam results.
I could hear the theater buzzing.
Why is everybody so restless?
The office kept buzzing until just before the announcement.

examples.ko: 모두 술렁대서 수업을 시작할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Everyone was so restless that we couldn't start class.

explain: '술렁거리다'와 같은 뜻이에요. 사람들이 웅성웅성하며 불안하거나 들떠 있을 때 써요. 더 짧은 '술렁이다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '술렁거리다'. It is used when people are murmuring, anxious or excited. The shorter '술렁이다' is also used.

examples.en: The fans were stirred up by the news about the new coach.
The market is suddenly in a stir.
The classroom starts buzzing when the announcement comes on.
The restless mood soon calmed down.

examples.ko: 마음이 술렁여서 일이 손에 안 잡혀요.
examples.en: My mind is restless, so I can't focus on my work.

examples.ko: 소문 때문에 동네가 술렁이는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems the neighborhood is stirred up because of the rumor.

explain: '술렁거리다', '술렁대다'와 뜻이 같지만 더 짧아요. 주로 '분위기가 술렁이다', '마음이 술렁이다'처럼 써요. 사람들이 놀라거나 불안해서 웅성거리는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It means the same as '술렁거리다' and '술렁대다' but is shorter. It is mostly used like '분위기가 술렁이다' or '마음이 술렁이다', with the feeling of people murmuring in surprise or anxiety.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 술수를 써서 계약을 따냈어요.
examples.en: He used a trick to win the contract.
Be careful not to fall for that kind of trick.
He doesn't play fair and only plays tricks.
I noticed the other side's trick and refused right away.
That kind of trick doesn't work for long.
A victory won by tricks isn't joyful.

explain: '꾀'와 달리 남을 속이는 나쁜 느낌이 강해요. '술수를 쓰다', '술수를 부리다', '술수에 넘어가다'처럼 자주 써요. '술책'과 비슷하고 둘 다 좋은 뜻으로는 안 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '꾀' (a clever idea), it strongly suggests deceiving others. It is common in '술수를 쓰다', '술수를 부리다' and '술수에 넘어가다'. It is close to '술책', and neither is used in a good sense.

examples.en: That ad is a ploy to deceive consumers.
I got caught up in the other side's scheme.

examples.ko: 할인 행사는 손님을 끌려는 술책이라고 보는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people see the sale as a ploy to attract customers.
That kind of scheme doesn't work anymore.
I heard the rival company is hatching a scheme.
Please tell me honestly, without any scheming.

explain: '술수'와 거의 같지만, '술책'은 미리 짜 둔 계획이라는 느낌이 더 강해요. '술책을 꾸미다', '술책에 말려들다'처럼 써요. 좋은 뜻으로는 안 써요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '술수', but '술책' has a stronger sense of a plan made in advance. It is used in '술책을 꾸미다' and '술책에 말려들다'. It is not used in a good sense.

examples.ko: 동생은 숫기가 없어서 낯선 사람과 말을 잘 못 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is shy and can't talk well with strangers.

examples.ko: 숫기 있는 친구가 먼저 말을 걸었어요.
examples.en: A friendly, outgoing friend spoke to me first.
The child who used to be shy has become much brighter.

examples.ko: 그렇게 숫기 없이 있으면 친구를 못 사귀어요.
examples.en: If you stay that shy, you can't make friends.
He is outgoing, so he mixes well anywhere.

examples.ko: 저는 숫기가 없는 편이라 발표가 힘들어요.
examples.en: I tend to be shy, so presentations are hard for me.

explain: 대부분 '숫기가 없다'로 쓰고, 낯선 사람 앞에서 쑥스러워서 말이나 행동이 서툰 모습을 말해요. '숫기가 있다/좋다'는 반대로 붙임성 있고 활발하다는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '숫기가 없다', describing someone awkward in speech and action out of bashfulness around strangers. '숫기가 있다/좋다' means the opposite: sociable and lively.

examples.ko: 칼을 다 갈았으면 숫돌을 물로 깨끗이 씻어 주세요.
examples.en: When you finish sharpening the knife, rinse the whetstone clean with water.
The knife was dull, so I sharpened it on a whetstone.
You have to wet the whetstone before using it.
Grandfather is sharpening a sickle with a whetstone.

examples.ko: 새로 산 숫돌이 아주 잘 갈려요.
examples.en: The whetstone I just bought sharpens very well.
The middle of the whetstone has worn down and become hollow.

explain: 칼이나 낫을 갈 때 쓰는 돌이고 '숫돌에 갈다'처럼 동사 '갈다'와 같이 써요. 요즘은 집에서 칼갈이 도구를 쓰는 경우도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the stone used to sharpen knives or sickles, and it pairs with the verb '갈다', as in '숫돌에 갈다'. Nowadays some people use a knife sharpener at home instead.

examples.ko: 그렇게 할 거면 숫제 안 하는 게 나아요.
examples.en: If you're going to do it like that, it's better not to do it at all.
Rather than do it half-heartedly, just quit altogether.

examples.ko: 그는 제 말을 숫제 듣지도 않았어요.
examples.en: He didn't even listen to me at all.

examples.ko: 밖에서 사 먹느니 숫제 집에서 만들어 보세요.
examples.en: Rather than buying it outside, why not just make it at home.

examples.ko: 기다리지 말고 숫제 직접 가 보는 게 어때요?
examples.en: Instead of waiting, how about just going there yourself?

examples.ko: 그 사람은 사과도 없이 숫제 모르는 척했어요.
examples.en: He didn't even apologize and acted as if he knew nothing.

explain: '아예'나 '차라리'와 비슷하고 '-느니 숫제'의 모양으로 자주 나와요. 어중간한 것보다 극단적인 쪽이 낫다고 할 때 써요. 말투가 조금 예스러워서 일상에서는 '아예·차라리'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is close to '아예' or '차라리' and often appears as '-느니 숫제'. It is used when you say an extreme choice is better than a halfway one. It sounds a bit old-fashioned, so in daily talk people also say '아예' or '차라리'.

examples.en: He is an ardent worshipper of this singer.
The hero's worshippers gathered in the square.

examples.ko: 저는 돈의 숭배자가 되고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to become a worshipper of money.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 숭배자도 많고 비판하는 사람도 많아요.
examples.en: That director has many admirers and many critics too.
He was always surrounded by his worshippers.
I was once a devoted admirer of my teacher too.

explain: '팬'보다 훨씬 강하고 거의 종교처럼 떠받드는 느낌이에요. 가벼운 좋아함에는 '팬'을 쓰고, 숭배자는 무조건 따르는 사람을 조금 비꼬듯이 말할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '팬' (fan), with a feeling of near-religious devotion. For light liking, use '팬'; 숭배자 can also be said a little sarcastically about someone who follows blindly.

examples.en: Our country has respected learning since long ago.
That society reveres strength.
People in the past had a strong reverence for filial piety.
Which values people esteem differs from person to person.
I grew up in a culture that has revered courage.

examples.ko: 조상을 숭상하는 전통이 아직 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The tradition of revering ancestors still remains.

explain: '존경하다'는 사람에게 많이 쓰고, 숭상하다는 학문, 힘, 효도처럼 가치나 문화를 높이 받들 때 써요. 말투가 딱딱해서 일상에서는 '중요하게 여기다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '존경하다' is mostly for people, while 숭상하다 is for lifting up values or culture, such as learning, strength or filial piety. It sounds stiff, so in daily talk people also say '중요하게 여기다'.

examples.en: I chopped the green onion in chunks and put it in the soup.
Please slice the potatoes into thick pieces.

examples.ko: 구멍이 숭숭 뚫린 치즈를 먹어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried cheese full of holes.
My socks have holes all over them.
It's an old house where the wind blows right through.
Cut the radish into chunks and put it in the steamed fish.

explain: 두 가지로 많이 써요. 채소를 큼직하게 썰 때 '숭숭 썰다', 구멍이 여러 개 난 모양을 말할 때 '구멍이 숭숭'이에요. 작고 가늘게 썰 때는 '송송'을 써요.
explain_en: It is used in two main ways: '숭숭 썰다' for cutting vegetables into big pieces, and '구멍이 숭숭' for something full of holes. For small, fine cuts, use '송송' instead.

examples.en: Mullet sashimi is delicious in winter.
I bought one mullet at the market.
A mullet jumped up at the river mouth.

examples.ko: 숭어는 바다와 강이 만나는 곳에서도 살아요.
examples.en: Mullet also live where the sea and a river meet.
I caught a mullet by fishing at the weekend.
Grilled mullet is tasty with just salt.

explain: 회나 구이로 먹는 생선이에요. 물 위로 잘 뛰어오르는 모습 때문에 속담에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 친구가 한다고 따라 하다니, 숭어가 뛰니까 망둥이도 뛴다더니 딱 그 말이네요.
phrases.en: Copying just because your friend does it—it's just like the saying 'when the mullet jumps, the goby jumps too.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 하니까 자기 형편은 생각하지 않고 무작정 따라 하는 사람을 놀릴 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb used to tease someone who blindly copies others without considering their own situation.

explain_en: It is a fish eaten as sashimi or grilled. Because it often leaps out of the water, it appears in a proverb.

examples.en: I met countless people on that road.
That actor has won awards countless times.
I had countless failures, but I didn't give up.
There were countless rumors about that singer.

examples.ko: 이 일을 하며 겪은 고생이 숱해서 말로 다 못 해요.
examples.en: I've been through so many hardships in this job that I can't put them all into words.
My many worries disappeared one by one.

explain: '많다'보다 글 같은 느낌이고, '숱한 실패', '숱한 밤'처럼 지나온 경험이나 사례가 아주 많다고 돌아볼 때 잘 어울려요. '숱하게 + 동사' 모양도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It feels more literary than '많다' and fits when looking back on very many experiences or cases, as in '숱한 실패' or '숱한 밤'. The '숱하게 + verb' pattern is also common.

examples.en: The company tried to hush up the accident.
It was embarrassing, so the family kept it quiet among themselves.
Hushing up a problem doesn't solve it.
Everyone knew, but the mood was to keep quiet about it.
Even if you hush it up, rumors spread quickly.
Please don't just hush that matter up and move on.

explain: 나쁜 일이나 잘못이 밖으로 알려지지 않게 조용히 덮을 때 써요. 대부분 비판하는 느낌이 있어요. 한 사람이 숨기는 것보다 여러 사람이 입을 닫는 장면에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when a bad thing or a mistake is quietly covered up so it doesn't get out. It usually carries a note of criticism. It fits scenes where several people keep their mouths shut better than one person hiding something.

examples.en: The child seems sleepy and slowly closes their eyes.
The door slid open softly.
The knot came undone by itself.
The snow melts away gently in the warm weather.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들으니 화가 스르르 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Hearing that, my anger just melted away.
I drifted off to sleep as soon as I sat on the sofa.

explain: 힘을 들이지 않고 부드럽게, 저절로 움직이거나 변하는 모습이에요. '스르르 잠들다', '스르르 녹다', '스르르 풀리다'처럼 자주 어울려요. '스르륵'은 같은 모양에 미끄러지는 소리가 조금 더 느껴지는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes something moving or changing smoothly by itself, without effort. It pairs often with '스르르 잠들다', '스르르 녹다' and '스르르 풀리다'. '스르륵' is the same image with a little more of the sound of sliding.

examples.en: The curtain slid open softly.
The snake slithered quietly into the grass.
The hair tie slipped loose.
I'm sleepy, and my eyelids are drooping.
The door closed softly.

examples.ko: 안심이 되자 몸에서 힘이 스르륵 빠졌어요.
examples.en: When I felt relieved, the strength drained from my body.

explain: '스르르'와 거의 같지만 무언가 살짝 스치듯 미끄러지는 소리와 느낌이 조금 더 들어 있어요. 문, 커튼, 매듭이 소리 없이 움직일 때나 힘이 빠질 때 써요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '스르르' but carries a bit more of the sound and feel of something sliding past lightly. It is used for doors, curtains and knots moving quietly, or for strength draining away.

examples.ko: 팔에 벌레가 기어가는 것처럼 스멀스멀 간지러워요.
examples.en: My arm feels creepy-itchy, as if a bug were crawling on it.

examples.ko: 등 뒤에서 이상한 기운이 스멀스멀 올라왔어요.
examples.en: A strange feeling crept up from behind my back.
An anxious feeling is slowly creeping up in me.
Smoke crept slowly into the room.
My scalp felt creepy-itchy, so I kept scratching it.

examples.ko: 아침이 되자 안개가 스멀스멀 퍼지고 있어요.
examples.en: As morning came, fog was slowly spreading.

explain: 벌레가 살갗 위를 기어가는 듯 근질근질한 느낌을 말해요. 비유로 불안, 연기, 안개 같은 것이 슬그머니 번지거나 올라오는 모습에도 자주 써요. '스멀스멀 올라오다', '스멀스멀 퍼지다'처럼 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes a tingly, itchy feeling as if a bug were crawling on the skin. Figuratively it is also used for anxiety, smoke or fog creeping in and spreading. It pairs with '스멀스멀 올라오다' and '스멀스멀 퍼지다'.
